## House card

## Lineage

Algirdas's second marriage (1350) to **Uliana of Tver** produced the inner dynasty: [Jogaila](../characters/jogaila.qmd) (c. 1362 – 1 Jun 1434; Władysław from 1386), [Skirgaila](../characters/skirgaila.qmd), Kaributas, Lengvenis, Karigaila, Vygantas and [Švitrigaila](../characters/svitrigaila.qmd). [Record]

Jogaila's four marriages: **Jadwiga of Anjou** (1386; one daughter, who died in infancy in 1399), **Anna of Celje** (1402; Jadwiga, 1408–31), **Elżbieta Granowska** (1417; none) and **Sophia of Halshany** (1422), mother of **Władysław III** (1424–44), **Casimir IV** (1427–92) and a short-lived Kazimierz. [Record] Sophia's family is the [Alšėniškiai](alseniskiai.qmd). Casimir was elected Grand Duke on 29 Jun 1440, aged 12, and crowned King of Poland on 25 Jun 1447.

## Feuds & alliances

Jogaila against Kęstutis (1380–82) and Vytautas (1382–84, 1389–92); Švitrigaila against everyone (1393, 1402, 1408, 1430–32); Skirgaila's resentment of Jogaila's ingratitude. Marriage web: Moscow (Lengvenis, Elena), Masovia (Aleksandra and [Siemowit IV](masovian_piasts.qmd)), Pomerania, Mecklenburg. After 1386 the house is also the Polish crown, and the Lesser Poland lords rule through it.

## Fate across the books

- **I:** Jogaila, bought by Henė, kills his uncle and agrees the Krėva Union (1385); baptised 1386. **II:** distant in Kraków; Skirgaila rules for him. **III:** reconciliation at Grunwald.
- **IV:** outlives Vytautas, still guilty; his sons come only from the last wife, and the lords sell their succession for privileges.
- **V:** Jogaila dies at Gródek (1 Jun 1434), Henė's last stone dropping. Casimir inherits both realms, and the Grand Duchy becomes a province of his house, as the bargain's letter said. [Saga]
